official.deadline_note: The scholarship follows the admission round, so there are two windows: master's admissions for autumn 2027 run 7 December 2026 - 5 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC+2), while English-taught bachelor's admissions (rounds A and B) run 7-22 January 2027. Master's applicants must have all documents uploaded by 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC+2).
official.status_note: The master's application period for studies beginning in autumn 2027 has not yet opened: Aalto states it 'will run from 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027', and the English-taught bachelor's period is 7-22 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are awarded as tuition fee waivers, covering the full tuition fee during the target time of the programme. Published tuition fees for rights to study beginning on or after 1 August 2025: bachelor's - business EUR 12 000 and technology EUR 12 000, art and architecture EUR 15 000 per academic year; master's - business EUR 15 000, technology EUR 17 000, multidisciplinary programmes EUR 17 000, art and architecture EUR 20 000 per academic year.
benefits: 100% tuition fee waiver covering the full tuition fee during the target time of the programme
Granted for the target time of the degree programme: three years full-time study for a bachelor's degree and two years for a master's degree
Continued to the second (or third in bachelor's) academic year subject to an annual study-progress review
Applying for the scholarship does not affect the admission decision; you may also decline it and still accept your study place
eligibility: Liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto University - most non-EU/non-EEA citizens of degree programmes taught in English
Applying for admission to a bachelor's or master's programme taught in English in the same application
Merit-based, granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria
EU/EEA citizens are not eligible, as they do not pay tuition fees and therefore cannot receive a tuition-fee waiver
Scholarship candidates are screened against the EU sanctions lists
requirements: Apply for the scholarship during the application period for admission; the scholarship application is part of the admission application form
Scholarship must be applied during the application period - it cannot be applied for afterwards
If awarded, agree to the terms of the scholarship by the given deadline for the scholarship to be valid
Full-time study and studying according to the approved personal study plan, with at least 45 ECTS per academic year to keep the residence permit renewable
documents: Application form in the Studyinfo.fi service with the scholarship option selected
Bachelor's degree certificate and official transcript of study records (master's applicants)
Copy of passport or official government-issued photo ID showing citizenship (non-Finnish citizens)
Accepted proof of English language proficiency sent/received by 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC+2)
Study-option-specific documents such as a portfolio (art, design, architecture) or GMAT/GRE scores (School of Business admission group 2)
All documents must be PDF, high-quality scans of originals, uploaded by the document deadline
selection_criteria: Applicants are ranked according to the criteria indicated on the study option's webpage
In master's admissions scholarships are allocated during the academic evaluation stage as part of the admissions process of a degree programme
The best applicants liable to tuition fees may be awarded a scholarship; programmes may decide not to grant any scholarships
Scholarship decisions are finalised before admission results are released and cannot be appealed under the Universities Act
coverage: Full tuition fee for the target time of the degree programme (three years full-time bachelor's, two years full-time master's)
EUR 12 000-20 000 per academic year depending on field and level, per the published tuition fee schedule
Does not cover living costs: 'Students need to cover all living expenses (at least 800 euros per month) and other study related costs from their own financial resources'
Does not cover personal study-related costs, the compulsory Student Union AYY membership fee or the FSHS student healthcare fee
Scholarships also apply during an exchange period or internship abroad, which the student continues to pay for out of the waived tuition
application_method: Read the application instructions and your study option's evaluation criteria before the period opens
Complete the application form in the national Studyinfo.fi service during the application period and select the scholarship option
Upload all application documents to the application form by the document deadline (12 January 2027 for master's)
Pay the EUR 100 application fee if not an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen
After the decision, accept the study place by the deadline and agree to the scholarship terms by the given deadline
official.application_route: Aalto's admission application in the national Studyinfo.fi service - tick the scholarship option on the same application form; there is no separate scholarship application and no second chance to apply later.
official.citizenship_residency: Only applicants liable to pay tuition fees may apply: most non-EU/non-EEA citizens of English-taught degree programmes. EU/EEA citizens, Swiss citizens and holders of fee-exempting Finnish residence permits (P, P-EU, EU Blue Card, certain A permits, family member residence card, Brexit permits, temporary protection) cannot receive the waiver.
official.international_eligibility: Yes for non-EU/non-EEA international applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees; EU/EEA citizens are explicitly not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field or agency restriction - every English-taught chargeable degree programme has its own evaluation criteria, and each programme may decide to award none at all
official.duration: Target time of the degree programme: three years full-time study for a bachelor's degree and two years full-time study for a master's degree
official.description: Aalto University describes the programme as seeking 'to recognize talented non-EU/non-EEA students across the world by awarding academic excellence'. Excellence Scholarships are awarded as tuition fee waivers covering the full tuition fee, applied for during the admission process, merit-based and highly competitive, with a very limited number available.
official.english_requirement: Master's taught in English: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with writing 6.0; TOEFL iBT taken on or after 21 January 2026 total 4.5 with 4.0 in all subtests (or taken before that date, total 92 with writing 22); PTE Academic overall 68 with writing 61; C1 Advanced grade A, B or C; YKI level 5; or an exemption such as a degree taught in English in a listed country. Applications without the required proof are rejected.

not_confirmed: A single fixed euro award amount - the award is a 100% waiver of the applicable tuition fee, published as a range of EUR 12 000-20 000 per academic year by field and level
A standalone scholarship deadline - the scholarship follows each admission round's application deadline
The number of scholarships available per programme, and which programmes will award any in this cycle

verification.notes: Amounts, coverage wording, deadlines and documents taken from five aalto.fi pages (scholarship page for study rights from 1 Aug 2025, scholarships and tuition fees, master's admissions, English bachelor's admissions, language requirements), all updated between September and October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a waiver, not a stipend: if you win it you pay zero tuition for the whole target time of your degree, but you still have to prove to Finland that you can live on at least EUR 800 a month before your residence permit is issued. Your chances are decided by the same academic evaluation that decides admission, so there is nothing extra to sell - the application tick-box is the entire scholarship application, and it is only open during the admission window. Apply to the programme whose evaluation criteria you genuinely match, because a second-choice option carry their own award that does not transfer if you are later admitted to your first choice from a waiting list.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A high-attaining non-EU/non-EEA applicant to an English-taught Aalto programme whose family budget genuinely covers Finland's living costs without any stipend.
application_readiness_checklist: Book the IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Cambridge test in early 2026 so the official score reaches Aalto electronically by 12 January 2027 at 15.00 UTC+2
Read your specific study option's evaluation criteria now and check whether it requires a portfolio, GMAT/GRE (School of Business, admission group 2) or an interview
Request an official, signed transcript of records and degree certificate from your registrar early; unofficial prints and student-system screenshots are rejected outright
Arrange an authorised translation into English, Finnish or Swedish for any credential issued in another language
Scan everything in the correct orientation as PDF and name the files exactly as Aalto's naming scheme requires
Prepare evidence of roughly EUR 800 per month of living funds plus the EUR 100 application fee, since the waiver does not touch them
common_rejection_risks: A mandatory document missing after the 12 January 2027 document deadline makes the application incomplete and it is rejected regardless of grades
English proof that never arrives from the test administrator - a PDF you upload yourself is not enough for TOEFL, PTE or IELTS verification
Being admitted from the waiting list: scholarship decisions are already final, so a later offer carries no waiver and no reallocation
In master's admissions, holding a scholarship tied to your second study option and losing it because you waited for your first choice
Weak or misaligned prior studies against the study option's own ranking criteria, which differ programme by programme
Falling below 45 ECTS per academic year, which both ends the waiver and puts the residence permit at risk
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs of at least EUR 800 per month in the Espoo-Helsinki region, flights and installation costs, study materials and computers, the compulsory Student Union AYY membership fee (EUR 65 in 2025-26) and the FSHS student healthcare fee (EUR 36 per semester in 2026), because Aalto publishes no university-wide living-cost award to offset them.
document_audit: A Diploma Supplement alone cannot replace a degree certificate; a provisional certificate is only accepted if it carries the name, degree, institution and award date no later than 31 July 2027
Transcripts must list courses, grades, credits and completion dates - missing grades need an extra official explanation of the grading system
Passport copies must show citizenship, and a passport expired more than 12 months before the application period will not be accepted
Translations must be produced by the awarding institution or an authorised translator bearing a stamp and signature; your own translation is not valid for school records
Applying to two study options means duplicating every option-specific document, including separate motivation letters and portfolios
alerts: The scholarship window closes with the admission window - once the application period ends there is no route to a tuition-fee waiver mid-studies
Scholarship decisions cannot be appealed under the Universities Act, so a missed tick-box or deadline is unrecoverable
In master's admissions the scholarship is study-option-specific and does not follow you if you are admitted elsewhere
Aalto reserves the right to change the scholarship programme and the tuition fee level, so re-check the fee schedule before you commit
Scholarship income in Finland is generally tax free only up to about EUR 26 269 per calendar year (2024 limit); if you also hold travel or living-expense grants the excess can become taxable
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one application form in Studyinfo.fi during the open window, tick the scholarship, upload every required document by 12 January 2027, pay the EUR 100 fee, then wait for the single decision that covers both admission and the award.
